conflicts.subject: charge-idempotency
conflicts.detail: A falls back to str(id(order)) as the idempotency key (not stable across retries or processes) and never checks whether the order is already paid, so a retry or a second pay with a new key charges the customer again. The user requires: never charge twice.
solutions: Require the client's key, bind it to one order, record the first attempt's key before calling the gateway and reuse it on every retry, and never charge an order that is already paid
Keep A's behaviour (rejected: breaks the user's requirement)
conflicts.recommended: Require the key; one gateway key per order, recorded before the call; no charge for a paid order

resolution.decision: The client's key is required (no str(id(order)) fallback) and bound to one order; the first attempt's key is written before the gateway is called and reused on every retry, so one order makes at most one gateway charge; an already-paid order is never charged again whatever key is sent

conflicts.subject: gateway-timeout
conflicts.detail: In A a gateway exception after the charge went through propagates and the order stays unpaid with no charge id, while the customer has been charged (the mock gateway's timeout_after_success does exactly this).
solutions: Retry once with the same key (the gateway is idempotent by key); if the outcome is still unknown leave the order pending with its attempt key so the next pay or the charge.succeeded webhook completes it
Mark the order paid on timeout (rejected: no charge id, may not have been charged)
conflicts.recommended: Retry with the same key, otherwise stay pending and let the next attempt or the webhook reconcile

resolution.decision: On a gateway timeout, retry once with the same key (the gateway is idempotent by key); if the outcome is still unknown the order stays pending with its attempt key and the error is raised; the next pay (any key) or the charge.succeeded webhook completes it without a second charge

conflicts.subject: webhook-idempotency
conflicts.detail: A applies every webhook delivery again and ignores the event type, so a redelivered or refund event marks the order paid again. The user requires: never apply a webhook twice.
solutions: Deduplicate by event id inside the same atomic write as the event's effect, and act by event type
Deduplicate by (order, type) only (rejected: a later legitimate event of the same type would be lost)
conflicts.recommended: Event-id dedupe in the same write as the effect; type-aware handling; no backwards moves

resolution.decision: Each event id is recorded in the same atomic write as its effect; a redelivered event does nothing; charge.succeeded and charge.refunded are handled by type; unknown types and orders are ignored; no backwards moves

conflicts.subject: cancel-paid-order
conflicts.detail: C cancels a paid order without refunding it (its own comment says so) and lets a cancelled or refunded order be cancelled again. The user requires: cancelling a paid order refunds it, exactly once.
solutions: Cancel of a paid order refunds its charge once through the gateway and ends in 'refunded'; cancel is a no-op on cancelled or refunded orders
Keep C's behaviour (rejected by the user's requirement)
conflicts.recommended: Refund once and end in 'refunded'; idempotent cancel

resolution.decision: Cancelling a pending order ends in 'cancelled'; cancelling a paid order refunds its charge through the gateway exactly once and ends in 'refunded' with one ledger refund; cancelling a cancelled or refunded order is a no-op

conflicts.subject: write-failure
conflicts.detail: No source persists anything or handles a failed write; the user requires that when a database write fails the order is left unchanged (StoreError) and the order stays consistent. A change spread over several writes, or a gateway call made before the record of it, could leave a charge or refund with no record.
solutions: Every state change is one atomic write (order, ledger entry and processed event id together); before calling the gateway, write the intent (attempt key or refund intent) so a failed write means the gateway is never called
Call the gateway first, then write (rejected: a failed write would leave money moved with no record)
conflicts.recommended: One atomic write per state change; intent written before any gateway call

resolution.decision: Every state change is one atomic store write (order, ledger entry, processed event id together); before any gateway call the intent (attempt key or refund intent) is written first, so when that write fails (StoreError) nothing is changed and the gateway is not called

conflicts.subject: order-payment-state
conflicts.detail: A records payment as a boolean 'paid'; C records it as status 'paid' among four states. Two fields for one fact can disagree (A's webhook sets paid=true on a refund event; C's cancel leaves paid=true on a cancelled order).
solutions: One status field with C's four values and a transition table; A's paid becomes status == 'paid'
Keep both fields in sync (rejected: two sources of truth)
conflicts.recommended: Single status field; paid is derived, not stored

resolution.decision: One status field with C's four values (pending, paid, cancelled, refunded) and an enforced transition table; A's paid flag is not stored (paid means status == 'paid')

conflicts.subject: renewal-duplicates
conflicts.detail: B creates a new order on every renew() call with no billing period, so a repeated renewal creates a second order, which would then be charged.
solutions: One order per subscription per period: a repeated renewal returns the existing order
Keep B's behaviour
conflicts.recommended: One order per subscription per period

resolution.decision: One order per subscription id per period: renewing again for the same period returns the existing order

conflicts.subject: order
conflicts.detail: Order exists in A:Order, C:Order; fields not shared: amount (only A), charge_id (only A), paid (only A), status (only C)
solutions: Merge into one table holding the fields kept features need
Keep separate tables if the two only share a name, and rename one
conflicts.recommended: Merge only once it is confirmed they mean the same thing; then list every field's origin in architecture.json

resolution.decision: Merge A:Order and C:Order into one Order (the user's task.md describes one order flowing from subscription to payment to cancellation); fields: id, customer, amount_cents (from A:Order.amount), status (from C:Order.status, replaces A:Order.paid), charge_id (from A), attempt_key, refund_state, refund_id

conflicts.subject: amount-units
conflicts.detail: A's order['amount'] and B's subscription['price'] have no stated unit; the mock gateway takes amount_cents and the user's API uses amount_cents.
solutions: Integer minor units (amount_cents) everywhere; reject non-integer or non-positive amounts
Decimal major units

resolution.decision: Integer minor units: amount_cents on orders, price_cents on subscriptions; non-integer, boolean or non-positive amounts are rejected

conflicts.subject: order.primary-key
conflicts.detail: Order primary key type is not known for A, C; find it before deciding the merged key
solutions: Read the source's schema or migrations for the type
Record it as unknown and decide in the architecture
conflicts.recommended: Find the real type before designing the merged entity

resolution.decision: Neither source has a key (in-memory dicts); the unified Order key is a string 'ord_<n>' generated by the app
